rule: Do not use an em dash or an en dash. Use a hyphen.
Percentages use the % sign, not the word percent or per cent.
Use the Oxford comma in a list of three or more items. Two items are not a list. Do not insert a comma into a phrase of two.
Use straight quotation marks. The account chooses single or double. Curly quotes are not used.

A count of things from zero up to the account's ceiling is in words. Always use numerals for a measurement with a unit, a percentage, money, a multiple, a date, a range, and every count above the ceiling. When a small count and a large count of the same thing are compared, both are numerals. A fund number, a series, a product name, a ticker, and a clause number keep their form.

A currency amount uses the ISO code before the amount. Write GBP for a pound sign and EUR for a euro sign. Write USD for a dollar sign unless the sources show another dollar (C$, A$, S$, HK$, or NZ$), in which case use that code. When the sources show more than one of those dollar codes, leave the dollar sign and say so.
Use the account's thousands separator in amounts. Do not put a thousands separator in a year. Do not flag a number that has no separator.
An amount of 1,000 million or more is written in billions to one decimal when the account chooses billions. Otherwise it stays in millions.
A date in prose uses the account's date form. Do not flag a month and a year with no day.
A quarter, a half, and a financial year are spelled out when the account chooses words. Otherwise use the short form. Spell a period only when it does not sit directly before the noun it describes.
Place a period after the noun it describes.
Link a derived figure explicitly. Do not leave it as a bare apposition or a bracket.
A year range uses a hyphen, except after from or between.
Use the account's spelling. A proper noun keeps its own spelling.
Write US and UK. Do not write U.S. or U.K.
After a capitalised name, a legal identifier is omitted or kept, as the account chooses.
Use the official name on first mention, then a shortened name when it is unambiguous. Capitalise a formal strategy or product name the same way throughout.
A job title is lower case when it is generic, and capitalised with a name.
Once a draft defines a term, later uses keep that form. Do not flag a term that was not defined. Lower case the before the defined noun is correct mid-sentence.
Write year on year, quarter on quarter, and month on month. Hyphenate only before a noun. When it is not clear that a noun follows, do not hyphenate. Do not write over.
Write manager, not general partner.
Write public market comparables, not listed comparables.
State a return as gross or net, then the multiple and the IRR, in that shape.
Do not write deal. Write transaction or investment.
Reporting commentary is third person. Investor letters and LinkedIn posts use we for the authoring organisation. A press release is third person, and we appears only inside quoted speech.
Prefer the active voice when the actor is known.
Do not use hype or a distinction claim. A measured qualitative word is allowed. Do not swap a hype word for a milder one that still praises.
Keep one register. Do not mix a formal sentence with slang.
Use short, clear sentences. Avoid a run-on.
Use plain words. Explain a specialist term on first use, or leave it out.
Do not use a word on the account's banned list.
